tips.title: Wash warm, rinse cool
tips.body: Hot water strips scalp oils and inflames dry scalps. Wash with lukewarm water and finish with a cooler rinse to help the cuticle lie flat.

tips.title: Blot, don't rub
tips.body: Wet hair is at its weakest. Rubbing with a towel snaps strands and roughs up the cuticle — blot and squeeze instead, ideally with microfiber.

tips.title: Shampoo is for the scalp
tips.body: Lather at the roots where oil and sweat live. The suds rinsing through the lengths is all the mid-shaft needs on most days.

tips.title: See a dermatologist early
tips.body: If your hairline or crown is visibly changing, the earlier you talk to a dermatologist, the more options you have. Clinically proven treatments exist — timing matters more than any product.

tips.title: Growth routines run on streaks
tips.body: Scalp serums and massage only show results after 8–12 weeks of near-daily use. Missing whole weeks resets the clock — build the habit first.

tips.title: Feed the follicle
tips.body: Hair is protein. Chronic low protein, iron or vitamin D shows up on your head months later. Fix the plate before buying a fourth serum.

tips.title: Stress sheds are real
tips.body: Big stress events can push hair into a resting phase and cause visible shedding 2–3 months later. It's usually temporary — manage the stress, keep the routine.

tips.title: Hats don't cause baldness
tips.body: A normal-fitting hat won't kill follicles — that's a myth. Very tight headwear worn daily can cause traction stress at the edges, so keep it comfortable.

tips.title: Pre-wet before the pool
tips.body: Hair soaked in tap water absorbs far less chlorinated water. Wet it at the poolside shower, and rinse again right after your swim.

tips.title: Sweat isn't dirt — but don't sleep in it
tips.body: After training, a water-only rinse and a quick scalp massage clears the salt without over-washing. Save the shampoo for your scheduled wash days.

tips.title: Keep the dryer moving
tips.body: Blow-dry on medium heat, nozzle 15 cm away, always moving. Concentrated heat on one spot does more damage than the tool itself.

tips.title: Scan like a scientist
tips.body: For hairline tracking, consistency beats quality: same mirror, same light, same distance, hair pulled back the same way. Change one variable and the trend gets noisy.

tips.title: Trim on a schedule
tips.body: Every 4–6 weeks for short cuts, 8–12 for longer styles. Regular trims keep ends from splitting upward and make growth look intentional.
